name: KAZAKHSTAN

flag.title: Sky & Sun
flag.note: Blue sky, gold sun & soaring eagle, 32 rays

lead: Kazakhstan is the world's biggest landlocked country. It has endless golden steppe and Tian Shan peaks. Nomads rode horses here for thousands of years and lived in round tents called yurts. Today rockets launch from Baikonur.

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Kazakhstan is as wide as Western Europe. Most of it is steppe, which is flat grassland. The south-east has jagged Tian Shan peaks. The west dips to 132 m below sea level.
The Aral Sea was once the world's fourth-largest lake. It shrank to 10% of its size when Soviet engineers diverted its rivers. A 2005 dam is refilling the north.
animals: The golden eagle is the national animal. Hunters called berkutchi have flown eagles from horseback for over 4,000 years. A golden eagle dives at 240 km/h.
The saiga antelope has a bulbous nose that filters dust and warms icy air. It was nearly extinct. Now over 2.8 million roam the steppe.
culture: Guests are fed first. The host gives the sheep's head to the most honoured visitor. Beshbarmak ('five fingers') is boiled horse or lamb on noodles, eaten by hand.
The dombra, a two-stringed lute, is the soul of the steppe. People have drunk kumiss, fermented mare's milk, for 5,000 years. They treat it as both drink and medicine.
history: Silk and spice caravans crossed Kazakh lands through Taraz and Otrar. Genghis Khan swept through in 1219. The Kazakh Khanate rose in the 15th century.
Russia took over Kazakhstan in the 18th–19th centuries. Soviet rule brought space launches from Baikonur. Kazakhstan declared independence on 16 December 1991, the last Soviet republic to do so.
wows: Kazakhstan is bigger than Western Europe but has no ocean coast.
DNA studies show the wild apple forests near Almaty gave us every apple.
Baikonur launched Sputnik in 1957 and Yuri Gagarin in 1961.
The ₸ symbol for the tenge was chosen in 2007.
Khan Tengri's marble summit glows blood-red at sunset.
Saiga numbers jumped from 50,000 to 2.8 million in two decades.
Astana's winters plunge to −40 °C, among the coldest for any capital.

myths.myth: Borat shows what Kazakhstan is really like
myths.fact: Borat was filmed in Romania. Real Kazakhstan has modern cities, and women vote and drive.

myths.myth: A lake is either fresh or salty
myths.fact: Kazakhstan's Lake Balkhash is half fresh water and half salty, split by a narrow strait.
